title: Antarctica Fly-Cruise in 12 Days: Sail the Drake Passage, Explore the Peninsula and Fly Back
meta_title: Antarctica Fly-Cruise 12 Days: Drake Passage and Peninsula
meta_description: 12-day luxury Antarctica fly-cruise from Santiago: sail the Drake Passage, 5 days on the Antarctic Peninsula and fly back from King George Island.
hero_alt: Snow-covered peaks and ice at the bottom of the world
tagline: Sail one way across the Drake, fly back over it
facts: Charter flights and an all-suite expedition ship
Active: Zodiac landings, walks, optional kayaking
intro: A luxury expedition voyage that sails one way and flies the other. A charter flight takes you from Santiago to Puerto Williams, the southernmost town in the world, where you board a small all-suite expedition ship. After two days crossing the Drake Passage you spend five days in the Antarctic Sound, on the Antarctic Peninsula and in the South Shetland Islands, with Zodiac cruises, landings and hikes every day and kayaking for experienced paddlers. From King George Island you fly back across the Drake in about 2 hours. Late February is the best time for whales and for penguin chicks before they go to sea. Because weather can delay the return flight from Antarctica, we strongly suggest an extra night in Santiago before your flight home.

best_time: The Antarctic season runs from November to March. November brings pristine snow and courting penguins; December and January have the longest days and penguin chicks; February and March are best for whales.
seasons: Fresh snow, sea ice and penguins building nests.

faqs.q: Why sail one way and fly the other?
faqs.a: You experience the Drake Passage by sea once, and save about two days by flying back. It suits travellers who want the full crossing but have limited time.

faqs.q: What if the flight cannot leave Antarctica?
faqs.a: You wait on the ship, warm and fed, until the weather clears. This is why we book your flight home at least a day after the tour ends.

faqs.q: Is it suitable for older travellers?
faqs.a: Yes, for those who can manage Zodiac boarding with help and short walks on uneven ground. The doctor on board must approve your medical form.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Fitness and medical
good_to_know.text: Landings are by inflatable Zodiac boat onto rocky or snowy shores, and there is no hospital in Antarctica. You must be able to climb in and out of a Zodiac with help and walk on uneven ground. The ship has a doctor.

good_to_know.title: Wildlife and the rules
good_to_know.text: Stay at least 5 m from penguins and seals and further from whales on the water; give animals right of way. Boots and gear are cleaned before and after each landing so no seeds or soil reach Antarctica. Take nothing and leave nothing.

good_to_know.title: Weather decides
good_to_know.text: Every landing, Zodiac cruise and the flight over the Drake Passage depend on the weather. The expedition leader may change the plan at short notice; flexibility is part of the journey.

good_to_know.title: Layers
good_to_know.text: An expedition parka and waterproof boots are provided. Bring thermal base layers, a fleece, waterproof trousers, warm gloves, a hat, sunglasses and high-factor sunscreen: the light off the ice is intense.

dining_intro: The ship's chefs cook vegetarian meals every day and can prepare Jain meals if told well in advance; we send your dietary brief at booking and again 60 days before sailing.
dining_avoid: Ask for vegetarian stocks and sauces, and confirm Jain meals with the restaurant manager on the first evening.
